correctness.rationale: Exact symbolic reduction from the three-compartment equations to a planar quadratic ODE was verified. Positivity, \(\dot i\le -m i^2\), and comparison against a scalar Riccati equation prove \(i,d\to0\). If total denier time were finite, an integrating factor gives \(i(t)\sim1/(mt)\), contradicting integration of \(\dot d+md\ge asi\). On the resulting divergent clock \(\tau=\int d\,dt\), the ratio \(r=i/d^2\) satisfies an exact asymptotically logistic identity. Logistic comparison, reciprocal-r integration at \(k=m\), and integrable logarithmic corrections at \(k>m\) establish all sharp constants and positive amplitudes. Exact symbolic and finite numerical checker tests corroborate, but do not substitute for the infinite-time argument.

The sharp infected laws \(t^{-2}\), \(t^{-2}/\log t\), and \(t^{-(1+k/m)}\), with their coefficients and global positive-state scope, were not established by that source. value.rationale: The motivating 2026 paper explicitly leaves critical exponents undetermined. Two of its phase boundaries meet at the natural codimension-two surface where both nontrivial eigenvalues vanish. The theorem classifies every initially infected homogeneous-mixing solution there, including a marginal \(t^{-2}/\log t\) law and a continuously varying fast-regime exponent \(1+\delta/\mu\). These answer a motivated quantitative question, with sharp coefficients and a globally attracting scope rather than an arbitrary finite slice; no stochastic-network universality is claimed.
